title: Measured methane-emission-factor summaries for biogas process stages and equipment
article_citation: Wechselberger, V.; Reinelt, T.; Yngvesson, J.; Scharfy, D.; Scheutz, C.; Huber-Humer, M.; Hrad, M. (2023). Methane losses from different biogas plant technologies. Waste Management, 157, 110–120.
license: CC BY 4.0 for the article; the Zenodo v1 dataset record also displays CC BY 4.0. Zenodo v2 reports the same data, but its record page does not display a separate rights statement.
source_location: Article Table 2, Presented study columns; footnotes a and f
derivation: Transcribed the 11 process/equipment rows and their sample counts, medians and reported ranges from Table 2. The table's Summary and Previous studies columns are excluded. Table 2 mean values are not provided for the Presented study rows and are therefore left blank.
study_scope: Harmonized on-site measurements at 33 biogas plants in Austria, Germany, Sweden and Switzerland. The plants primarily treated energy crops, manure, biowaste or wastewater sludge.
basis_rule: Table 2 footnote a: methane slip from biogas utilization/upgrading is expressed as percent of methane utilized; other emissions are expressed as percent of methane produced.
sample_size_definition: n_reported transcribes Table 2 N for the Presented study column; it counts reported measurement data points and must not be interpreted as an independent population sample unless the source says so.
applicability: Cross-technology comparator for Phase 5 AD emissions, Phase 6 upgrading methane slip, Phase 7 digestate-storage emissions and LCA methane-emission completeness. Not a roadside-grass or GreenHub installation measurement.
limitations: The 33-plant study does not investigate GreenHub grass-derived process gas or digestate; the feedstocks and plant contexts differ.
Technology-specific measurement counts are small for several rows. Medians and ranges are not probability distributions and are not GreenHub defaults.

For the PSA row, the paper's Table 2 footnote says measurements were upstream of exhaust-gas treatment and that the treatment was out of order; do not treat the value as final PSA-system slip with functioning exhaust treatment.
The article reports that membrane-separation upgrading was not covered by the study; no membrane row is included in this extract.
The data are equipment/component methane-emission factors, not a whole-plant leakage factor. Do not sum rows without matching system configuration and preventing overlap.
The extract contains article Table 2 aggregates only; it does not reproduce the 294-point underlying repository data.
